t: LeetCode 3258 – Count Substrings That Satisfy K-Constraint I
o: Count substrings of a binary string where the zeros ≤ k OR the ones ≤ k. With |s| ≤ 50, checking all O(n²) substrings works, but the cleaner view: for a fixed right endpoint, validity is monotone in the left endpoint (shrinking the window can only help), so the invalid left endpoints form a prefix — a two-pointer sweep counts valid substrings ending at each r in amortized O(1). For '10101', k = 1 the counts per right endpoint are 1, 2, 3, 3, 3 → 12.
k: Validity is monotone as the window shrinks, enabling two pointers.
Valid substrings ending at r = r − l₀ + 1 where l₀ is the smallest invalid left index.

a.i: Expand r, maintaining zero/one counts; while BOTH counts exceed k, shrink from the left. Afterwards every left index ≥ l gives a valid substring, contributing r − l + 1.
s: For each r: add s[r] to counts; while z > k and o > k, remove s[l] and advance l.
a.t: O(n) — each index enters and leaves the window once

a.n: Approach 2: Brute force over all substrings
a.i: Enumerate every (i, j), maintain running zero/one counts, and accept when either count ≤ k. Perfectly adequate at n ≤ 50 and a good correctness reference.
s: For each start i, reset counts.
Extend j, updating counts; count the substring if z ≤ k or o ≤ k.

w: Give the brute force in one sentence, then present the two-pointer as the real solution (it also scales to the n = 5·10^4 version of this problem). Pitfall: the shrink condition is AND (both counts exceed k), not OR — the OR lives in the definition of validity, and invalidity is the conjunction. Follow-up: the harder version asks for substrings also bounded in length, requiring a monotonic queue over window lefts.
